proposal:
SCOPE. Hand-derived; nothing executed. One unimplemented root rule, SSR (stabilizer-section restriction), replaces BLQ's greedy basis and 2^n certificate with a canonical construction and a polynomial syntactic check. It exploits one tractable family: CNFs with a nontrivial syntactic translation stabilizer. It is not a SAT algorithm and bounds no solver trace.

OBSERVATION. If F(x)=G(πx) with π linear and λ a right inverse, then G=F∘λ. Choosing λ as a coordinate embedding makes the quotient a plain restriction of F. So no fresh variables, basis choice or compatibility test are needed.

RULE. Blocks are exact-support forbidden-point sets (S_B,B).
(1) Remove subsumed clauses first. Deployed BLQ runs before Canon, so one superset clause creates a one-point block and destroys symmetry.
(2) U_B={t: B+t=B}. Candidates are p0+q for q∈B, so cost is O(|B|²w) with no 2^|S| enumeration.
(3) K={k∈F2^n: k|S_B∈U_B for all B}, W=K^⊥, r=dim W.
(4) Put W in RREF. J=non-pivot columns, |J|=n−r, and K projects bijectively onto F2^J.
(5) If r<n, assign x_J=0 and keep surviving variables in original relative order. Repeat to a fixpoint (merged blocks can create new symmetry; ≤n rounds). Lifting extends a model by zeros.

CERTIFICATE. Generators k_1..k_s and J, with two checks: B+k_j|S_B=B for every block and generator, and (k_j)_J invertible. Hand-counted cost is O(s·L) plus one elimination, where L is total literals. One generic Lean theorem (T22) would cover every instance instead of per-instance 2^n proofs. The existing enumeration stays as a cross-check for n≤12.

LEDGER (T23, hand-proved). Block B becomes exactly |B|/2^|S_B∩J| clauses of width |S_B∖J|. Clause count and width never increase, and output size is known beforehand. Any blockwise linear quotient has rank ≥r, so SSR matches BLQ's variable count whenever BLQ accepts and accepts whenever r<n. 'Incompatible greedy basis' is no longer a possible outcome.

GROWTH INVARIANT. Record (n,r,ledger) at root for every fixture. If r=n the formula is syntactically translation-rigid, the skip is real and the peak belongs to the solver. If r<n and compression skipped, it is a compression failure.

INDEPENDENT-TEST PREDICTIONS (for an SSR prototype, not the deployed solver).
P1. auto00006: r=6, 9 binary clauses on 6 variables, equal to the deployed quotient up to renaming.
P2. auto00007: r=4, 6 binary clauses. P1 and P2 rest on my earlier hand decoding.
P3. Triangle T on variables 1..6: block {1,2,3} forbids its 4 even-weight points, block {4,5,6} likewise, block {1..6} forbids its 32 even-weight points. 40 clauses, UNSAT. From the brief's greedy description I infer deployed BLQ skips: it picks the two weight-3 forms, and the width-6 block owns no chosen form. SSR gives r=2, J={2,3,5,6}, output exactly (x1)(x4)(x1∨x4)(¬x1∨¬x4), refuted by unit propagation. Ledger: 4→1, 4→1, 32→2.
P4. Neon 00045: by hand, K=0. The two 2-point width-8 blocks have stabilizers ⟨e5+e6+e7+e8⟩ and ⟨e9+e10+e11⟩, forcing k1..k4=0 and k12=0; the triple parities then kill the rest. SSR skips, matching the receipt's no_dimension_reduction. Composed with FMA (00040): G=first 96 clauses, dim K=8, μ*=4/256=1/64, J={5..12}, output (x1∨x2)(¬x3∨¬x4)(¬x1∨x3)(¬x2∨x4)(¬x1∨x4)(¬x2∨x3), UNSAT.
P5. auto00008: not in this brief, not decoded. If r<11, SSR outputs exactly r variables and ≤88 clauses. If r=11 the formula is rigid and the greedy label hides a rank fact. I predict no peak either way.
FALSIFIERS: an SSR output failing the 2^n check, a ledger mismatch, or deployed BLQ accepting with fewer than r variables.
missing_theorem:
T22 (first; Lean target; hand-proved, not machine-checked). Let k_1..k_s satisfy B+k_j|S_B=B for every block, with (k_j)_J invertible. Then for every c∈F2^J, SAT(F)⟺SAT(F|x_J=c), and any model of the restriction extended by c satisfies F. Proof: F∘τ_k=F on the span; for a model x choose k with k_J=x_J+c.

T23 (hand-proved; Lean target).
(i) K_S⊆U_B maps onto F2^(S∩J) and B is K_S-invariant, so the fibres of B over F2^(S∩J) are translates of each other. Hence the restricted block has |B|/2^|S∩J| points.
(ii) ker π⊆K for every blockwise linear quotient π, so rank π≥r.
(iii) For subsumption-free F, 'every translated clause is subsumed by a clause of F' coincides with exact invariance, so step (1) loses nothing.

BARRIER (hand-proved). φ(x)∧z is invariant under flipping z iff φ is UNSAT, so membership in the semantic stabilizer is coNP-hard. SSR is complete only for the syntactic stabilizer of the subsumption-reduced clause set.

T24 (first open). Section choice. The ledger Σ_B |B|·2^(−|S_B∩J|) depends on the information set J. With K=⟨e1+e2+e3⟩ and a block on {1,2}, J={3} removes nothing and J={1} halves it. Matroid greedy maximizes the linear proxy Σ_{j∈J} occ(j) exactly (Rado–Edmonds). The exact ledger is a supermodular minimization over matroid bases. I conjecture it is NP-hard and claim only the proxy.

T25 (open, possibly false). peak(F|x_J=0)≤peak(F) for the deployed ELIM rule. Receipts show clause changes move peaks non-monotonically. No work bound follows from SSR until this is settled.
self_attack:
1. Known territory. This is variable-flip (phase-shift) symmetry breaking by restricting to a transversal. The contribution is limited to identifying it with BLQ, the canonical section, the ledger and the polynomial certificate. Where BLQ already accepts, SSR yields nothing new.
2. auto00008 is unseen. r may be 11, making SSR useless there. Or r<11 and the restricted formula may still peak 16; a full-rank parity system stays awkward for clause-count-bounded DP. I have not shown SSR lowers any measured peak.
3. No extra-clause robustness of its own. One width-n clause forbidding one point makes any formula rigid, and leaves satisfiability unchanged when |K|≥2. Robustness comes only from FMA, including its weakness on narrow blocks (36+9: μ*=9/4) and punctures.
4. Syntactic only. Re-encoding by resolution or cube merging, beyond plain subsumption, hides the symmetry. An adversary moves the class boundary cheaply.
5. Nonlinear gadgets (auto00009) are untouched: a one-point perturbation makes the block odd.
6. Costs are hand counts, not measurements. Lean kernel evaluation of the polynomial check may still be slow.
7. Restriction changes the solver's context. T25 may fail, so SSR could raise a peak. Section choice is open.
8. P3's 'deployed skips' is an inference from the brief's wording. If the greedy rule picks the width-6 form, T only tests agreement.
9. All hardness lives at r=n. The invariant classifies instances; it bounds nothing. No universal claim.
mechanism_signature: SSR | unimplemented | root-only, after literal normalization and subsumption; replaces BLQ discovery, greedy basis and 2^n check | K = ∩_B preimage(Stab(B)), W = K^⊥, J = non-pivot columns of RREF(W) | certificate: generators k_j with B+k_j|S=B for all blocks and (k_j)_J invertible | action: assign x_J=0, original relative order, iterate to fixpoint | exact ledger |B|→|B|/2^|S∩J|, width −|S∩J| | check O(s·L) by hand count, no enumeration | optional FMA pre-split F=G⊔R with μ*<1 | no claim on rigid instances, punctures, nonlinear gadgets or solver work
delta_from_prior: FMA (00040) used 'deployed BLQ accepts G' as its guard. It therefore inherited the greedy incompatibility skip, the 12-variable 2^n certificate and the fresh-variable construction. SSR replaces that guard. New here: quotient = restriction, the RREF section, the polynomial syntactic certificate, the exact ledger, rank minimality, subsumption-before-symmetry ordering, the coNP barrier for semantic stabilizers, and the (n,r) record separating compression failure from solver hardness. New test: triangle T. New decoding: 00045's extras are two 2-point blocks, K=0 by hand, and FMA∘SSR gives μ*=1/64. Nothing here addresses punctures, narrow-block extras or nonlinear gadgets.
